scope: Stylized synthetic air-support operator; not an empirical sortie-effect model.
question: How much durable insurgent suppression does information-conditioned air support add per unit of government resource cost, and how does the frontier change as civilian-harm sensitivity rises?
internal_cost_scale: 600 capital units equals 0.5% of the default 120,000 monthly federal policy-budget ceiling. This is an internal model opportunity-cost scale, not a real-dollar estimate.
mechanism: Domestic military support is available only when that formation detects its opponent.
Government capital cost = support_level*600 per supported contact.
Civilian harm is multiplied by 1 + support_level*specified harm multiplier.
No additional RNG is consumed; intensity zero follows the baseline branch.
analysis_rules: Use intensity0 as baseline within each seed.
Report suppression per 100,000 capital spent separately by insurgent outcome.
Report Pareto frontier across suppression, government losses, civilian harm/displacement, and cost.
Estimate diminishing returns across support intensity.
Do not collapse civilian harm and suppression into one utility score.
selection_guard: All 15 cells frozen before fresh outcomes. Any alternate firepower coefficient/cost scale requires new seeds.
interpretation_guard: Synthetic support tradeoff only; not an operational airpower recommendation.
